jobs.title: Water Resources Coordinator/EIT
jobs.description:
At HDR, our employee-owners are fully engaged in creating a welcoming environment where each of us is valued and respected, a place where everyone is empowered to bring their authentic selves and novel ideas to work every day. As we foster a culture of inclusion throughout our company and within our communities, we constantly ask ourselves: What is our impact on the world?

Watch Our Story:' https://www.hdrinc.com/our-story'

Each and every role throughout our organization makes a difference in our ability to change the world for the better. Read further to learn how you could help make great things possible not only in your community, but around the world.

We believe water is more than a resource, it's a shared responsibility. As part of our Water Business Group, you’ll help shape how communities manage water for generations to come. From delivering safe drinking water and treating wastewater responsibly to developing sustainable water supplies and protecting lives and property through flood control, your work will directly support public health, environmental sustainability, and infrastructure resilience. We bring together experts across disciplines to solve complex challenges with bold thinking and technical excellence. Whether you're modernizing aging systems or pioneering innovative approaches, your contributions will make a meaningful difference in people’s lives. This isn’t just a job, it's a chance to lead change, drive progress, and leave a lasting legacy.

We believe water is more than a resource, it's a shared responsibility. As part of our Water Business Group, you’ll help shape how communities manage water for generations to come. From delivering safe drinking water and treating wastewater responsibly to developing sustainable water supplies and protecting lives and property through flood control, your work will directly support public health, environmental sustainability, and infrastructure resilience. We bring together experts across disciplines to solve complex challenges with bold thinking and technical excellence. Whether you're modernizing aging systems or pioneering innovative approaches, your contributions will make a meaningful difference in people’s lives. This isn’t just a job, it's a chance to lead change, drive progress, and leave a lasting legacy.

HDR is looking for an Engineer In Training to join our Water Resources team in Sacramento, CA. Candidates for the position should have technical experience in water supply, flood risk management, coastal storm risk management, environmental restoration, inland and deep draft navigation infrastructure projects and experience in watershed scale feasibility studies/assessments for the federal government (ex. USACE, Bureau of Reclamation). Our clients include local, state, and federal agencies.

Our team is growing and has a range of challenging and innovating projects. We work within multi-disciplinary teams on projects related to flood management; water supply and system operations modeling; reservoir operations; hydropower system analysis; decision support systems for water management; FIRO and water control manual development; hydrology development and analysis; ensemble and statistical analysis; FERC relicensing, and ecological enhancement. The preferred candidate would have experience in a combination of these subject areas.

The candidate is expected to be a key part of project delivery teams, mentor junior staff; manage small- to medium-sized projects, and effectively interact with clients and peers. Candidates should be able to work independently, but also enjoy working in a collaborative team environment. The candidate must have strong writing skills and good quality control/quality assurance processes. This candidate will also perform other duties as assigned.

In the role of Water Resources Engineer-in-Training (EIT), we'll count on you to:

Support medium- to large-size planning, reservoir operation, and environmental compliance projects on behalf of the federal government
Prepare, plan and analyze compliance documents
Work with others in completion of required studies, documents and reports
Demonstrate public participation, agency coordination, planning and programming experience
Perform other duties as needed

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Studies, Hydrology, Civil Engineering, Water Resources or closely related field
Graduate Degree
Familiarity with reservoir and system modeling, water supply operations modeling
Experience with water infrastructure planning studies, extreme hydrology, and/or consequence analysis
Experience with risk-based planning and risk-informed decision making
Familiarity with integration of resiliency into the planning process

Benefits: Employee Stock Ownership, Medical insurance, Dental insurance, Vision insurance, 401(k), Paid time off (PTO), Paid holidays, Paid parental leave, Life insurance, Disability insurance.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering or equivalent field
Experienced with Microsoft Office Suite, standard CAD platforms such as AutoCAD, and hydraulic modeling software
Self-motivated, able to work independently and with a project team to completion of task
An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture is a must

What We Believe

HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

Our Commitment

As employee owners, we all have a role in creating an inclusive environment where each of us is welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to bring our authentic selves to work every day.

Our eight Employee Network Groups (Asian Pacific, Black, Hispanic/Latino(a), LGBTQ+, People with Disabilities, Veterans, Women, Young Professionals) help create a sense of belonging and foster a supportive environment where everyone is empowered to engage and contribute. Each group has an executive sponsor and is open to all employees.

We provide a comprehensive benefits package that promotes employee ownership, employee health, performance, and success, which includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, life insurance, an employee assistance program, paid time away, parental leave, paid holidays, a retirement savings plan with employer match, employee referral bonus and tuition reimbursement. Stated benefits are for full-time regular positions. The expected compensation range for this position is $71,082.00 - $101,545.00 annually depending upon skills, experience, education and geographical location. Primary Location:
United States-California-Sacramento Other Locations:
United States-California-Walnut Creek Industry:

jobs.title: Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
As the EHS Specialist
, you will help guide a comprehensive Environmental, Health and Safety program for the PPG Cleveland facility. You will provide direction and training to provide a safe and healthful workplace. You will ensure compliance with applicable environmental, health, and safety laws and regulations to minimize all liabilities/risk. You will have close interaction with all levels of the manufacturing, technical and engineering organizations.

The EHS Specialist will report to the site EHS Manager. Come join our team!

Main Responsibilities

Ensure compliance with Federal, State, Local and PPG environmental regulations and policies.
Maintain compliance with a Title V and multiple smaller air permits.
Manage water permits (Industrial and Stormwater), Waste Management Program (Hazardous, Non-Hazardous, Universal) for both Large and Small Quantity Generator(s).
Maintain emergency response and contingency plans.
Compliance with ISO14001 requirements; EPCRA Reporting (SARA 312 and SARA 313) and, improving of the environmental management process.
Participate in our facilities Emergency Response Teams (ERT).
Develop leading indicators that improve sustainability metrics (energy, water, waste) and spill incidents.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Engineering or related Science.
3+ years' experience in the EHS field, preferred manufacturing or chemical setting.
Knowledge of safety and environmental regulations and standards (OSHA, EPA, DOT, NIOSH, ANSI, NFPA, and Workers' Compensation).

The base salary range for this position is $100,000 - $125,000 with a possibility of an annual bonus up to 10% of base salary.

PPG offers comprehensive benefits such as Health, Dental, Life, Retirement Plan, Paid Vacation and Holidays, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Disability/Leave, Family Leave and other Voluntary benefit offerings. Actual benefit offerings confirmed at the time of hire.

jobs.description:
Benefits

Health insurance
Opportunity for advancement
Training & development
Vision insurance
Bonus based on performance
Company car
Competitive salary
Dental insurance

SERVPRO Team Wilson is looking for an experienced, dependable Mold Remediation Supervisor
to lead mold remediation projects from initial setup through completion. This is a hands-on leadership position for someone who understands restoration work, can lead technicians in the field, and takes pride in completing jobs safely, efficiently, and professionally.

The Mold Supervisor will work directly with project management and field technicians to ensure each project follows SERVPRO standards, proper remediation procedures, safety requirements, and customer expectations.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and supervise mold remediation projects in residential and commercial properties
Direct technicians and assign daily job-site responsibilities
Perform hands-on remediation work alongside the team when needed
Set up and maintain containment and negative-air environments
Properly operate air scrubbers, HEPA vacuums, dehumidifiers, and other remediation equipment
Perform selective demolition and removal of affected drywall, insulation, flooring, and other materials
Ensure proper PPE and safety procedures are followed on every project
Monitor job progress and communicate updates to Project Managers and Operations leadership
Document job-site conditions, work performed, equipment, and project progress
Maintain clean, organized, and professional job sites
Communicate professionally with homeowners, property managers, and other customers
Train, coach, and develop Mold Technicians
Ensure equipment and company vehicles are properly maintained and accounted for
Respond to emergency restoration needs, including occasional after-hours and weekend work

Qualifications

Preferred:

Previous mold remediation, water mitigation, environmental remediation, or restoration experience
Previous experience leading or supervising technicians
Knowledge of containment, negative air, HEPA filtration, demolition, and remediation procedures
IICRC certifications such as AMRT and/or WRT
Experience working for SERVPRO or another restoration company
OSHA, HAZWOPER, asbestos, or other environmental/safety training
Experience documenting restoration projects

Required

Strong leadership and communication skills
Ability to perform physically demanding work
Comfortable working in crawlspaces, attics, confined areas, and potentially contaminated environments
Ability to lift and carry restoration equipment and building materials
Strong attention to safety and detail
Valid driver's license and acceptable driving record
Ability to work both independently and as part of a team
Ability to participate in an on-call or emergency-response schedule when needed

What We're Looking For

The ideal candidate is someone who can lead from the front
. We aren't looking for a supervisor who only gives instructions—we need someone willing to work alongside the team, teach technicians the right way to perform remediation, maintain high standards, and take ownership of the job.

Successful Candidates Will Be

Dependable and accountable
Safety-minded
Comfortable leading people
Hands-on and mechanically inclined
Customer-focused
Organized and detail-oriented
Coachable and willing to follow SERVPRO processes
Interested in building a long-term career within the restoration industry

Compensation

Competitive hourly or salaried compensation based on restoration experience, certifications, and leadership background.

Benefits and additional compensation opportunities may be available based on position and location.

About SERVPRO Team Wilson

SERVPRO Team Wilson provides restoration and reconstruction services to residential and commercial customers following water, fire, mold, storm, and other property damage.

Our goal is to develop strong teams, provide opportunities for advancement, and deliver a high level of service to our customers.

SERVPRO Team Wilson is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Compensation: $24.00 - $28.00 per hour

Picture yourself here fulfilling your potential! Who is SERVPRO Team Wilson?

We are family-owned and operated business that has been serving the restoration needs of our community for many years. As a family, we believe in the importance of hard work, dedication, and treating our clients and employees like members of our own family. These values have helped us become one of the most successful teams in the SERVPRO system, as we strive to exceed our client's expectations and provide our employees with a supportive and rewarding work environment. We take pride in our reputation for excellence and are committed to continuing to deliver the highest level of service to our clients.

All employees of a SERVPRO® Franchise are hired by, employed by, and under the sole supervision and control of an independently owned and operated SERVPRO® Franchise. SERVPRO® Franchise employees are not employed by, jointly employed by, agents of, or under the supervision or control of Servpro Franchisor, LLC, in any manner whatsoever.

jobs.title: Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
Environmental Specialist

Triumvirate Environmental, one of the largest environmental services firms in North America, is seeking an Environmental Specialist for our
Lab & Onsite Support Services (Lab/OSS)
team. As an Environmental Specialist, you will support our clients on-site by managing their hazardous waste programs & projects, utilizing state & federal regulations.  
Triumvirate Environmental provides leading organizations in the higher education, life sciences, healthcare, and advanced manufacturing sectors with diverse services and expertise to assist them with compliance management. At Triumvirate Environmental, we strive to WOW both our employees and our customers. Our unique culture fosters growth, development, education, and creativity.    
This position reports to the Operations Manager. This role is based on site at client locations in the Astoria, NY area .

We invite you to watch this video to discover more about the exciting responsibilities of an Environmental Specialist at Triumvirate Environmental.
CLICK HERE

Responsibilities:

Develop an understanding of OSHA regulations as well as Triumvirate’s Health and Safety practices 
Preparation of chemical and biological waste for shipment and disposal, including creation of all federal/state waste documents and managing the paperwork for the material. 
Safe handling of hazardous waste containers on client sites, as well as loading/unloading of waste from vehicles 
Conduct safety equipment and hazardous waste inspections. 
Occasionally perform and document Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) audits for clients. 
Deliver Exceptional Customer Service: Champion our commitment to the WOW! by providing outstanding support and innovative solutions to our clients 
Develop a high-level of state and federal regulatory expertise ensuring our client’s compliance needs are met (e.g RCRA, DOT, and OSHA) 
Conduct spill response measures, including the assessment of the spills and cleanup efforts 
Rotating on-call responsibilities as part of our Emergency Response team 

Basic Requirements
:  
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in the hazardous-waste industry, or relevant military experience 
Ability to work as a member of a team as well as individually 
Must demonstrate strong verbal and written communication abilities to effectively interact with clients, colleagues, and stakeholders, ensuring clear and professional exchanges of information 
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex issues, develop solutions, and implement strategies to achieve positive outcomes 
Skilled in building strong, positive relationships with clients and colleagues 
Ability to work overtime on a regular basis 
Must be willing to work flexible hours within the work week (Monday through Friday) 
Ability to complete a 2 to 3 year professional advancement program in hazardous waste management 
The Environmental Specialist frequently handles hazardous chemicals and biological waste and is responsible for putting on and taking off personal protective equipment. This role is considered safety-sensitive 
Must be able to report to the office within 1 hour during Emergency Response rotating shifts 
Valid US driver’s license 
Must have a reliable form of transportation 
Must be willing to consent to  pre-employment physical and drug screen (inclusive of THC) 
Upon employment, you will be required to participate in a random drug screening program (inclusive of THC) as part of our company’s commitment to maintaining a safe and healthy work environment 
Must be eligible to work in the United States without future sponsorship 
Must be able to lift 60 pounds on a regular basis 
Upon employment must be willing to obtain a Commercial Drivers License (CDL)

Preferred Requirements:

Prior relevant industry experience 
Prior successful experience in a customer service role 
Active HAZWOPER 24 or 40 hour certification 

Besides Health, Dental and Vision Insurance, we contribute to a 401k, offer a generous tuition reimbursement program, TONS of safety training for some positions with opportunities for external trainings and certifications, Mentorship & Career Succession Planning, Relocation Opportunities, Auto/Home insurance discounts, pet assistance discount plans, discounted movie passes & more!    
To learn more about our business, culture, and the exciting work that we are doing in the industry, find us on LinkedIn, Instagram (@triumvirateenvironmental), or our website !   
Triumvirate Environmental is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. As an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE), Triumvirate does not discriminate based on race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Individuals with Disabilities and Protected Veterans are encouraged to apply.  
If you have a disability and need accommodation during the application and hiring process, please contact us at https://www.triumvirate.com/contact or call us at 888-834-9697.  The requirements listed above are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. To view our California Privacy Notice and Policy, click here .  

Actual starting base pay may vary based on factors such as education, experience, skills, location and budget.
Pay Range: $25 USD - $25 USD

jobs.title: Risk Assessment Privacy Specialist
jobs.description:
Ironwall by Incogni
is an executive privacy and protection service built for organizations that need to protect their most exposed people. We help companies and institutions reduce security risks to executives and other high-profile individuals by continuously finding and removing their personal information from the internet.

Role Overview

The Risk Assessment Specialist is responsible for conducting comprehensive Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) research to identify, analyze, and document publicly available information that may expose individuals to privacy, security, or personal safety risks.

This role involves researching multiple online sources, identifying personal information exposures, evaluating potential risks based on established assessment criteria, and developing detailed Risk Assessment reports that provide clients with a clear understanding of their digital exposure.

Key Responsibilities

Conduct OSINT research across search engines, data broker websites, people search platforms, public records, social media platforms, and other publicly accessible online sources.
Identify and document exposed personal information.
Analyze findings to determine potential privacy, security, and physical safety risks.
Evaluate exposure levels and assign risk scores based on established methodologies and guidelines.
Create comprehensive and well structured Risk Assessment reports, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and attention to detail.
Provide relevant insights and recommendations to help individuals understand and reduce their exposure.
Verify research findings and ensure all information included in reports is properly documented and supported by reliable sources.

Required Skills 

Strong online research and information-gathering capabilities.
Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
Excellent analytical thinking and investigative research skills.
Ability to identify patterns and connections between different pieces of information.
Strong written communication skills.
Ability to interpret findings and assess potential risks.
Strong organizational and time management skills.
Ability to work independently while following established processes and guidelines.
Understanding of online privacy, digital footprints, and information security is an advantage.

What Makes Someone Successful in This Role

The successful candidate is naturally investigative and enjoys connecting information across multiple sources. They are comfortable spending time researching, validating details, and identifying potential exposure risks that others might overlook.
They understand that seemingly unrelated pieces of publicly available information can collectively create meaningful privacy and security concerns. Most importantly, they can turn their research into accurate, organized, and actionable reports that help protect individuals.

Here's the deal:

Meaningful work:
Help protect people's personal information and reduce the risks of online exposure, fraud, cybercrime, and other threats.
Growth & development:
Join a growing company where you'll gain experience in privacy operations, online research, cybersecurity, and data protection.
Team environment:
Work remotely with a collaborative team that values ownership, accountability, and supporting one another.

Compensation:
MXN $300,000 per year plus benefits.

Ready to join us?

If you're detail-oriented, reliable, fluent in English, and passionate about protecting people's privacy, we'd love to hear from you.
Location:
Mexico
Work Arrangement:
Remote

Regulatory Toxicologist (Project)

Principal Scientist OR AD-level

Comp
175- 220k
MUST BE DABT certified

Job Summary

The Project and Regulatory Toxicologist will be expected to use his/her toxicology expertise to guide safety assessment, design, and interpret in vitro/in vivo studies to evaluate the safety profiles of our covalently and non-covalently targeted small molecules according to regulatory guidelines. You will work closely with the toxicology function, CROs, and multidisciplinary drug discovery/development teams to progress promising therapeutics to the clinic.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Represent the toxicology function as a subject matter expert on drug discovery and development project teams, and provide guidance on the safety characterization, prioritization, and advancement of drug candidates
Directly interface with CROs to place appropriate in vitro and in vivo toxicology studies in a timely manner; manage and oversee the execution of toxicology studies at CROs to ensure high-quality data delivery; review and QC study protocols, results, and study reports; summarize toxicology study results and communicate findings to project teams and senior management accurately and punctually
Contribute to the writing of safety study summaries, nonclinical overviews, and other regulatory documents; represent the company at regulatory interactions
Identify and implement new strategies on safety assessment to address current and future safety-related challenges as needed; keep abreast of current regulatory requirements by participating in cross-industry consortia or scientific conferences
Collaborate with early discovery project teams to conduct literature-based target safety assessments and provide guidance on target safety derisking activities

Education and Experience Requirements
Ph.D. in pharmacology, toxicology, or a closely related biomedical discipline with 6+ years of industry experience, or M.S. in the above field with 10+ years of industry experience
Diplomate of the American Board of Toxicology is highly desired
A broad understanding of various aspects of nonclinical safety assessment and regulatory requirements for drug development; experience representing the toxicology function on discovery and development teams is required; expertise in immunology is highly desired
Must be able to critically evaluate, interpret, and integrate multidisciplinary data to support target and compound safety assessment and mechanistic derisking
Experience in the design, conduct, and data interpretation of in vitro and in vivo safety pharmacology, genetic toxicology, and general toxicology studies is required
Experience working with CROs

Required Key Attributes
Excellent interpersonal skills, with the ability to interact professionally and effectively in a dynamic, multidisciplinary, and highly collaborative team environment
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Solid problem-solving skills with a strong sense of urgency and scientific curiosity
Proactive and agile, with the ability to operate in a fast-paced work setting
Solution- and result-oriented with attention to detail

jobs.title: Principal Environmental Compliance Consultant
jobs.description:
Terraphase offers cost-effective solutions to complex environmental and engineering challenges. We listen to our clients and focus on their needs. We apply technical expertise and keen awareness of the regulatory framework to achieve our clients' project goals and objectives. The combined talent and experience of Terraphase's engineers, geologists, and scientists form the foundation for a comprehensive environmental management approach.

The Opportunity

Founded in 2010, Terraphase Engineering is a dynamic, privately owned environmental consulting firm seeking a Principal Environmental Compliance Consultant—Scientist, Geologist, or Engineer—with 18 or more years of professional experience to help lead, grow, and support our Compliance Services Division.

Compliance is one of Terraphase’s four core service areas, alongside Environmental, Site Engineering, and Water Resources. As one of our fastest-growing service areas, the division is central to Terraphase’s long-term growth strategy, with dedicated resources and leadership focused on expanding our capabilities and reach.

This is a senior leadership opportunity for a proven seller-doer who combines technical expertise, established client relationships, and sound business judgment. We are looking for a senior colleague to partner with our national compliance leadership, bring an active book of business, and take a meaningful role in serving and expanding Terraphase’s existing client base.

At Terraphase, you’ll enjoy the personal attention and entrepreneurial culture of a small-to-mid-sized firm with fewer than 200 people, supported by multidisciplinary resources and offices across the United States. You’ll have the opportunity to help shape strategy, develop your client portfolio, mentor emerging leaders, and deliver practical solutions that help clients manage risk, improve operations, and meet their environmental obligations.

A Flexible Senior-Level Role

We recognize that accomplished professionals may be looking for different ways to contribute at this stage of their careers. We welcome candidates seeking either full-time employment or a meaningful part-time leadership role.

The position may be based at any Terraphase office nationally. Candidates outside our existing office markets are also encouraged to apply; alternative locations and remote or hybrid arrangements will be considered where a mutually agreeable business and working arrangement can be established.

Much of the senior-level work involves technical direction, desktop review, client relationships, and team leadership. Responsibilities, availability, business development expectations, and project commitments will be aligned with the agreed schedule and role. Travel will be based on client, project, and team needs.

The Role

Partner with national compliance leadership to expand the practice, identify priority opportunities, and help shape its long-term growth strategy.
Maintain and grow an established portfolio of client relationships while actively supporting Terraphase’s existing clients and compliance programs.
Develop new business through professional relationships, referrals, industry engagement, and targeted pursuits, and identify opportunities to expand services within existing accounts.
Maintain comprehensive knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental requirements, including state-specific regulations in California, Washington, New Jersey, and Texas, and federal programs under the Clean Water Act, RCRA, Clean Air Act, EPCRA, and related authorities. Translate these requirements into practical compliance strategies for clients operating across multiple jurisdictions.
Lead large-scale, multisite, and multistate compliance programs, translating complex requirements into practical actions that fit client operations.
Serve as a trusted advisor to corporate leaders, environmental managers, and facility personnel, including guiding regulatory negotiations and agency interactions.
Direct projects involving compliance audits, gap analyses, discharge monitoring, hazardous waste and materials management, stormwater and wastewater, tank and spill prevention programs, air quality, litigation support, and permitting, consistent with your technical expertise.
Help clients prioritize findings, implement corrective actions, and develop effective approaches to ongoing compliance management.
Develop proposals, scopes of work, budgets, and schedules, and lead responses to small and large requests for proposals and statements of qualifications.
Support project bidding, contract solicitation, and pursuit strategy while maintaining realistic commitments for staffing, technical delivery, and profitability.
Oversee and mentor consultants, scientists, and engineers, and manage subcontractors and vendors.
Help project managers and emerging leaders develop their client management, business development, and technical leadership skills.
Provide quality assurance and technical review of reports, plans, specifications, and other deliverables.
Monitor regulatory developments and industry trends to anticipate client needs and identify appropriate service opportunities.
Collaborate across offices and disciplines to deliver coordinated, cost-effective solutions and connect clients with Terraphase’s broader capabilities.

Who You Are

You have 18 or more years of relevant professional experience focused on environmental compliance, including substantial experience in consulting. Candidates currently working in industry or other leadership roles who have prior consulting experience are welcome.
You hold a bachelor’s degree in engineering, geology, environmental science, or a related discipline.
You bring an established book of business and active client relationships, supported by a demonstrated record of generating and delivering consulting work.
You are interested in both developing your own client portfolio and taking responsibility for serving and growing an existing client base.
You have demonstrated success leading complex compliance programs, managing client portfolios, and balancing business development with project execution.
You offer recognized expertise in one or more environmental compliance disciplines and a strong understanding of federal and multistate regulatory frameworks.
You can connect technical recommendations with clients’ operational priorities, business objectives, and risk management needs.
You communicate effectively with clients, regulators, technical teams, and business leaders, including through proposals, presentations, and negotiations.
You are a collaborative leader who mentors others, shares opportunities across teams, and maintains high standards for technical quality, client service, and professional integrity.

Preferred Qualifications And Skills

Relevant professional licensure or certification, such as PE, PG, or CHMM, or demonstrated subject matter leadership in areas such as hazardous waste, stormwater, air quality, or other compliance disciplines.
Experience developing and managing national or regional client programs, including consistent approaches to compliance across multiple facilities.
Experience with environmental management systems, compliance tracking, or tools that help clients manage recurring obligations and corrective actions.
Familiarity with government platforms such as EPA CDX, CERS, RCRAInfo/myRCRAid, TRI-MEweb, ECHO, E-Plan, and similar compliance systems.
Familiarity with, or experience leading teams who use, ArcGIS, Power BI, AutoCAD, and comparable tools.
Participation in professional associations, technical presentations, or other activities that build industry relationships and demonstrate technical leadership.

Compensation for this position is based on years of experience, technical expertise, technical education, and geographic location.

Pay Range: $135,000 USD - $200,000 USD

Who We Are

We are an environmental consulting company that offers cost-effective solutions to complex environmental and engineering challenges. We apply technical expertise and keen awareness of the regulatory framework to achieve our clients' project goals and objectives. The combined talent and experience of Terraphase's engineers, geologists, and scientists form the foundation for a comprehensive environmental management approach.

Terraphase was founded with the goal of developing a full-service engineering and consulting firm that provides high-quality services to clients with regional and nationwide operations. We are driven by creating valuable work products for our company and clients, and a rewarding environment for our employees. Our staff is comprised of registered professionals in civil engineering, geology, hydrogeology, and geotechnical engineering.

Our unique company culture philosophy of appreciating and recognizing individuals for their work, leadership, and mentoring, while supporting and encouraging a healthy personal and professional lifestyle help to make Terraphase one of the best places to work.

Benefits

Terraphase offers an extensive benefits package including; Medical, Dental, Vision, Employer Paid Life Insurance, Long-Term Disability, a generous 401(k) match, Commuter Benefits, TerraLunches, TerraTalks, Tuition/Licensing/Professional Development Reimbursement, Flexible Work Schedule, ongoing company-sponsored events.

EOE STATEMENT

Terraphase is an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to an inclusive & diverse work environment where individual strengths and diverse viewpoints are respected and complement each other to achieve common goals. (EOE M/V/F/D)

Under the direction of the Director and higher-level Environmental Scientists, responsible for managing programs and projects in support of environmental compliance and permitting for the Companies which may include, but are not limited to, environmental audits, environmental compliance training program, Environmental, Social Governance (ESG) environmental metrics, Greenhouse Gas (GHG) analyses. Participates in Company emergency response activities as assigned, including any activities required to prepare for such emergency response.

Working knowledge of continuous improvement principles, principles, procedures, tools, and desired behaviors.

Positive leadership and interpersonal skills.

In-depth analytical, investigative, and computational skills. Ability to apply problem-solving techniques to resolve problems and issues.
Ability to think creatively and strategically, and exercise independent judgment and initiative within established policy and guidelines.
Ability to be proactive, self-starting, and remain flexible in a demanding work environment, while adapting to rapidly changing requirements.

The ideal candidate demonstrates strong technical and communication skills, initiative, attention to detail, and the ability to work collaboratively across multiple environmental programs.

Performs responsible technical and scientific work conducting environmental fieldwork, monitoring, inspections, and related activities to maintain regulatory compliance at the County's solid waste facilities. This position requires familiarity with applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations, including Chapters 62-701 through 62-722, Florida Administrative Code (F.A.C.), governing solid waste management.

Supports multiple environmental programs and participates in cross-training to provide backup coverage for other team members, maintain continuity of services, and respond to changing operational needs.

Work is performed with considerable independence under the general supervision of the designated supervisor.

Representative Duties/Assignments

The duties listed below are representative of the position and may vary based on operational needs and assigned responsibilities. The employee is expected to develop proficiency across multiple environmental programs and provide backup support to other team members as needed.

Performs environmental fieldwork including groundwater, surface water, wastewater, soil, and air sampling; environmental monitoring; data collection; equipment calibration and maintenance; and various inspections.
Reviews field and analytical data for compliance with regulatory requirements and assists in preparing reports and documentation for submission to regulatory agencies.
Conducts compliance inspections of landfill and transfer station facilities, including random load inspections, landfill liner integrity inspections, and other inspections required by environmental permits.

Assists in developing and maintaining standard operating procedures, operational guidelines, and environmental compliance documentation.
Coordinates with operations personnel, consultants, contractors, and regulatory agencies regarding environmental monitoring and compliance activities.

Performs other related duties as assigned.

Such assignments may be for before, during or after an emergency/disaster.

Graduation from an accredited four (4) year college or university with major course work in environmental or civil engineering, the natural sciences, or a related field and one (1) year environmental experience; or an equivalent combination of education, training or experience.

Must be able to perform job related tasks, which would include but not be limited to: climbing, walking over uneven ground, exposure to dust and fumes, and occasional exposure to adverse weather.

Experience in environmental fieldwork, regulatory compliance, or hazardous waste management.

Job Summary

This role involves drafting State Implementation Plans (SIPs) as mandated by the Clean Air Act. This includes developing pollutant-specific nonattainment areas, infrastructure, and rule-based SIPs, as well as other regulatory required reports to be submitted to the U.S. EPA. You will also perform moderately complex legal analysis to support the rule writing process. This includes assisting in planning the overall rule development strategy, drafting rules, synthesizing information into clear and concise rule language, providing guidance on rule language and impact, and conducting outreach and engagement related to rule development.

This position is available for remote work on a full-time basis within Arizona (including virtual office arrangements).

The State of Arizona strives for a work culture that affords employees flexibility, autonomy, and trust. Across our many agencies, boards, and commissions, many State employees participate in the State’s Remote Work Program and are able to work remotely in their homes, in offices, and in hoteling spaces. All work, including remote work, should be performed within Arizona unless an exception is properly authorized in advance.

Job Duties

Develop SIPs: Utilize accurate air quality data, control analysis methodologies, and technical modeling demonstrations to complete defensible SIPs.

Conduct Policy Analysis: Perform complex policy analyses referencing EPA guidance, other state level air regulations, and case law.

Draft Environmental Regulations: Write and coordinate with the ADEQ Office of Administrative Council, the Governor’s office, and the Governor’s Regulatory Review Council to finalize and issue state environmental regulations.

Engage with the Public: Coordinate and host public meetings, hearings, and presentations for the regulated community and general public.

Internal Collaboration: Work closely with other ADEQ Sections focused on air quality data assessment and monitoring, air quality permits, and air quality compliance to ensure SIPs and state rules are based on and contain accurate data, relevant regulations, and applicable compliance methodologies.

External Collaboration: Work closely with federal and local state agencies, including U.S. EPA, local air pollution control agencies, tribes, cities, counties, etc., regulated facilities, and stakeholders to draft data driven SIPs and state rules with the objective of achieving measurable pollution reduction.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities (KSAs)

Knowledge of: federal and state environmental rules and regulations, the Clean Air Act, and regulations governing administrative procedures.

Skill in: legal research and writing, project management, and understanding unfamiliar topic areas in order to educate management on those topics.

Ability to: understand rules and statutes; follow guidance documents and standard operating procedures; draft state rules and State Implementation Plans; ensure accuracy in legal research, citation, and formatting while maintaining an objective and impartial tone; prepare clear, concise, and accurate reports; as well as summarize completed tasks and air monitoring data orally and in written communication.

Selective Preference(s)

Bachelor’s degree or higher in fields such as law, public policy, environmental and/or natural resource policy, environmental/chemical engineering, environmental science, atmospheric chemistry, meteorology, environmental resource management or a related field preferred, but not required.

Juris Doctor Degree or a Paralegal Degree or Certification is preferred but not required.

Job Overview

Our Clean Room Services team is looking for both entry level and veteran Environmental Monitoring Analysts that are passionate about leveraging their talents to provide an outstanding customer experience. If you’re interested in receiving excellent training and working as part of a team of experts with opportunities for growth, you’ll be a great fit in our strong company culture.

As a Cleanroom Services Analyst you will perform environmental monitoring and cleanroom qualifications within controlled environments. You will travel to regional client sites to provide your expertise with equipment, procedures, policies and regulations to ensure that their cleanrooms meet the requirements for safe manufacturing of medical devices, pharmaceuticals and other patient products.

Responsibilities

Expert use of scientific equipment while following policies and procedures
Measure total air particulate, temperature, humidity and differential pressure
Collect viable air and surface samples
Collect purified water samples for testing
Incubate media plates and enumerate any microbial growth
Submit growth for microbial identification per procedure and client instruction
Maintain and prepare equipment in a GMP environment.
Prepare and complete documentation (paper and electronic) per GDP.
Transport equipment and media to client sites within the New England region in company provided vehicles
Familiarization with client cleanroom layouts, sampling plans and contamination control programs
Sterile gowning and staging equipment and media into client cleanrooms for testing
Other duties as assigned
You will work with team members and under the direction of Cleanroom Services management to improve performance and client satisfaction.

Experienced Analysts will also - Perform compressed gas testing - Perform HEPA filter testing - Write risk assessments, sampling plans, investigations, protocols, reports, SOPs and other technical documents - Design and build electronic workflows - Peer review data - Assist with training - Cross-train to support other business functions, which may include: Validations, Metrology, Microbiology, Quality Assurance, Sales Support and Leadership

Qualifications/Skills

Ability to read, analyze, interpret, and follow standard operating procedures, technical procedures, professional journals and governmental regulations to provide advantage to Cambrex opportunities.
Mathematical skills including the ability to analyze scientific and test data, and a basic understanding of statistical analysis.
Ability to effectively present information to internal and external audiences.
Ability to write reports and business correspondences
Actively participate in team and company meetings.
Excellent interpersonal skills, with ability to interact effectively and work efficiently with customers, partners and colleagues at all levels in an organization.
Excellent communication skills: verbal, written and active listening.

Education, Experience & Licensing Requirements

Entry Level Qualifications

Associate’s degree in Microbiology or related field with a minimum of 12 months of working in a clean room environment-OR- High School Diploma or equivalent will be considered with a minimum of 24 months of working in a clean room environment
Sterile gowning experience preferred
Maintains a valid driver’s license and has a good driving record.

Expert Level Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree or higher in Microbiology or related field
Minimum of 12 months of sterile gowning experience
Minimum of 12 months of environmental monitoring sampling and testing experience
CETA or NEBB training / certification preferred
Employees in this role must be able to obtain and use a company-authorized payment method, such as a company credit card or fleet fuel card, to purchase fuel and other approved business expenses.

The estimated hourly rate range of $25-29/hour reflects an anticipated range for the CRS Analyst I position. The estimated hourly rate range of $27-$32/hour reflects an anticipated range for the CRS Analyst II position The estimated hourly rate range of $30-35/hour reflects an anticipated range for the CRS Analyst III position The actual hourly rate offered may depend on a variety of factors, including the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, specific and unique skills, level of education attained, and certifications or other professional licenses held. The actual hourly rate offered will be in accordance with state or local minimum wage requirements for the job location.

All requirements are subject to possible modifications to reasonably accommodate individuals with disabilities.

Cambrex is an Equal Opportunity / Affirmative Action employer and will consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, protected veteran status, or disability status.

Travel:
This role frequently performs work at client sites, so travel to and from client sites is part of the typical workday. Company vans are provided for travel to client sites, most of which are in southern New England. Approximately 10% of assignments are multi-day requiring overnight accommodation.

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee

to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be

made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee may be required to use hands to finger,

handle, or feel and to reach with hands and arms. The employee is required to talk and hear. The

employee is frequently required to stand, walk and sit. The employee may be occasionally required

to climb or balance. The employee may be required to regularly lift and/or move up to 10 pounds,

frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.

Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, and peripheral

vision.

Environment And Protective Equipment

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee

encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may

be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee may be occasionally exposed to moving

mechanical parts, high precarious places and vibration. The noise level in the work environment is

for inspections or work discussions. The employee is required to wear the appropriate personal

protective equipment to perform the job duties. Such personal protective equipment may include

gloves, etc.

jobs.title: Hazardous Materials Specialist
jobs.description:
What's The Role And What You'll Do

See the risk. Find the solution. Protect the community.

A chemical inventory tells you what a business stores. A site inspection tells you a bigger story.

Are incompatible materials stored together? Does the emergency plan reflect what is actually happening on site? Would first responders have the information they need when it matters most?

If those are the questions that get your attention, bring your curiosity, technical knowledge, and practical judgment to the City of Mountain View.

As our Hazardous Materials Specialist
, you’ll help businesses operate safely, support firefighters with technical expertise, and protect the people and places that make up our community. Reporting to the Fire Marshal in the Fire and Environmental Protection Division, you’ll connect science, fieldwork, education, and enforcement with opportunities to see the direct impact of your work.

Picture your workday

Your morning might begin with reviewing hazardous materials business plans in the California Environmental Reporting System (CERS) for the sites that will be inspected. This includes familiarizing yourself with the site and their prior inspection history.

Later, you head into the field. An inspection gives you the chance to compare the paperwork with actual conditions, evaluate potential hazards, and explain corrective actions in clear, practical terms.

Back at the office, you could review construction plans, document inspection findings, or coordinate with another agency on a regulatory question. When a hazardous materials emergency occurs, you may be called on to provide technical guidance to the Incident Commander.

Across these assignments, your judgment matters and so does your ability to help people understand and act on it.

Real work. Visible impact.

Your Assignments Will Connect You With Work Such As

Safer business operations: Review hazardous materials business plans, process permits, and help facilities understand and meet applicable requirements.
Underground storage tank oversight: Inspect monitoring systems, installations, and removals to evaluate compliance.
Construction and facility changes: Review proposed construction and hazardous materials facility closure plans for compliance with applicable requirements.
Field inspections and follow-through: Investigate concerns, document findings, explain necessary corrections, and take enforcement action when needed.
Emergency readiness and response: Educate firefighters, City employees, and industry safety personnel, and provide technical expertise during hazardous materials incidents.

The Essentials

Bring your science. Bring your people skills.

You can recognize a chemical hazard and explain why it matters to someone without your technical background. You ask thoughtful questions, write clear reports, and remain steady when circumstances change.

You understand that effective compliance takes both professional relationships and consistent follow-through. You’re comfortable helping someone work through a complicated requirement, and you can be firm when a condition needs to be corrected.

Relevant experience may come from hazardous materials compliance, environmental consulting, laboratory or industrial chemical safety, or other work involving hazardous materials storage and handling. Tell us how your background prepares you for this role.

Why bring your expertise to Mountain View? Help make innovation safe.

Mountain View is a place where people come to develop ideas, build businesses, and shape what comes next. As our Hazardous Materials Specialist, you’ll help create the conditions for that work to happen safely—with attention to the people handling hazardous materials, the firefighters responding to emergencies, and the community around them.

Here, your expertise reaches across the life of a facility: from reviewing proposed construction and hazardous materials business plans to conducting inspections, guiding corrective actions, and reviewing closure plans. You’ll have opportunities to understand how a business operates, identify what needs to change, and help turn a technical requirement into a practical solution.

You’ll also bring that knowledge directly into the Fire Department. Reporting to the Fire Marshal, you’ll support prevention efforts, help prepare first responders, and provide technical guidance during hazardous materials emergencies.

For someone who enjoys science, fieldwork, and working with people, that combination offers a compelling opportunity: build your expertise while seeing how your decisions help protect a whole community.

View the full job description here: Hazardous Materials Specialist

Are We a Match?

What You’ll Need

The classification calls for education equivalent to a bachelor’s degree in chemistry, biology, fire science/fire technology, or an environmentally related field, plus two years of recent full-time experience dealing with the storage and/or handling of hazardous materials. A combination of relevant experience, education, and training that satisfies the required qualifications will be considered.

Education, experience, and knowledge involving local, State, or Federal hazardous materials and fire prevention codes and regulations are also required.

You’ll need a valid California driver license upon appointment. Within six months of appointment, you must complete California Peace Officer Standards and Training PC 832 training and obtain ICC California Underground Storage Tank Inspector certification.

This position includes enforcement activities and response to hazardous materials emergencies. Work may involve strenuous physical effort, unpleasant environments, and potentially significant and unpredictable hazards.

Compensation

Full range $167,726 to $226,924 annually, with a control point of $197,325. Starting salary is flexible within the range based on experience, specialized expertise, and internal equity. The anticipated hiring range for this position is $167,726 to $197,325; i nitial salary placement will be based on the selected candidate’s qualifications, relevant experience, and alignment with the position.

Apply Now

Put Your Expertise To Work For a Whole Community.

If you enjoy connecting technical details to practical solutions and want your work to help keep businesses, first responders, and the public safe we invite you to bring that perspective to Mountain View.

About Atlas

Atlas is a trusted leader in environmental and infrastructure consulting services; we provide services that enable communities to flourish and thrive. With a team of 3,500 employees and offices throughout the US, we combine local expertise and a network of relationships to deliver solutions to both public and private clients. Our services help improve the quality of life in the communities where we live and work. We always aim for smart, safe, and sustainable results. At Atlas we understand that our future is everyone’s responsibility, and we create a better experience at every stage of a project.

Job Description

Launch your career in environmental consulting by working on projects that help assess, clean up, and redevelop properties across the region. You'll gain hands-on experience in the field and office while learning from experienced professionals and making a meaningful impact on communities and the environment. We're looking for an enthusiastic, self-motivated individual who is eager to learn and grow. Success means developing strong technical skills, safely supporting field and office activities, and becoming a reliable member of our project team.

Core Responsibilities

Support environmental site investigations by collecting soil, groundwater, soil-vapor, and other environmental samples.
Conduct and document field activities, including soil borings, monitoring-well installations, and underground storage-tank excavations or removals.

Assist with proposals, work plans, environmental reports, permit applications, and site-specific health and safety plans.
Maintain accurate field notes, project records, and documentation in accordance with Atlas quality and safety practices.
Coordinate multiple assignments and communicate progress, field observations, and potential concerns to project team members.

You’ll thrive here if you have

A bachelor’s degree in geology, engineering, environmental science, or a related field.
Up to two years of relevant environmental consulting, field, laboratory, or academic experience. Georgia-specific experience is helpful but not required.
A strong commitment to performing fieldwork safely and producing accurate, well-documented work.
Technical, analytical, research, and problem-solving skills, with proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
The ability to communicate clearly, work independently with appropriate guidance, and contribute to a collaborative team.
A valid driver’s license and driving record that meet company requirements.
The ability to perform moderately strenuous field activities and travel overnight, primarily within the state, approximately 20% to 30% of the time.

Job Responsibilities

Under broad supervision, directs, manages, and evaluates countywide environmental health programs and personnel within the Division of Environmental Health. Provides leadership and oversight of regulatory, permitting, inspection, enforcement, and public health protection activities while ensuring compliance with applicable local, state, and federal laws, regulations, and policies. Serves as a technical expert, program administrator, and liaison to governmental agencies, regulated industries, community stakeholders, and the public.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Program Administration and Leadership

Directs, plans, develops, implements, and evaluates countywide environmental health programs and services, which may include retail food service, onsite sewage management, and vector control.
Develops, reviews, updates, and implements program policies, procedures, and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
Evaluates program performance, goals, and objectives and implements improvements to promote effective service delivery, operational efficiency, and regulatory compliance.
Assists with strategic planning, program development, resource allocation, and the establishment of program priorities.
Monitors program operations to ensure consistent service delivery and adherence to established standards.

Regulatory Compliance and Enforcement

Interprets, applies, and enforces applicable local, state, and federal environmental health laws, regulations, codes, and policies.
Directs and oversees plan reviews, permitting, inspections, monitoring, complaint investigations, and enforcement activities involving retail food service operations and other assigned environmental health programs.
Oversees administrative and legal enforcement actions, as appropriate, to address violations and protect public health.
Ensures consistent application of regulatory requirements, inspection standards, and compliance procedures across environmental health programs.
Provides guidance on complex regulatory matters and assists staff in resolving compliance issues.

Staff Management and Development

Supervises and manages a team of approximately three to four Environmental Health Specialists.
Provides leadership, training, mentoring, performance feedback, and daily work direction to assigned personnel.
Conducts performance evaluations and establishes expectations for employee performance and professional development.
Oversees staff development, continuing education, and in-service training activities.
Participates in recruitment, selection, employee discipline, and other personnel management activities.
Promotes accountability, teamwork, professional conduct, and consistent application of program standards.

Public Health Response and Investigations

Oversees investigations involving foodborne illness outbreaks, disease transmission, and other environmental health incidents.
Directs responses to environmental health emergencies, public health hazards, environmental nuisances, and citizen complaints.
Coordinates response activities with public health officials, healthcare providers, emergency management agencies, and state and federal partners.
Provides technical guidance and administrative oversight during environmental health incidents requiring coordinated public health intervention.
Ensures appropriate documentation, follow-up, and resolution of environmental health investigations.

Technical Consultation and Stakeholder Engagement

Provides technical guidance, regulatory interpretation, and professional consultation on environmental health matters.
Serves as a technical expert and advisor to staff, local governments, state and federal agencies, regulated industries, consultants, and the public.
Represents the Division before community organizations, professional associations, governmental bodies, committees, and public meetings.
Develops and maintains effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Communicates regulatory requirements, program expectations, and public health recommendations to diverse audiences.

Administrative Responsibilities

Oversees environmental health inspection, permitting, reporting, and data management systems.
Reviews and prepares program reports, recommendations, presentations, correspondence, and other administrative documents.
Monitors program activities and documentation to support operational accountability and regulatory compliance.
Performs other related duties as assigned.

Required Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Knowledge

Thorough knowledge of environmental health programs, regulatory processes, and public health protection principles.
Thorough knowledge of applicable environmental health laws, regulations, codes, policies, and enforcement procedures.
Comprehensive knowledge of management, supervision, strategic planning, and program evaluation.
Knowledge of public health emergency response, outbreak investigation, and risk communication practices.
Knowledge of environmental health inspection, permitting, monitoring, and compliance activities.

Skills And Abilities

Ability to interpret and apply complex laws, regulations, policies, and technical standards.
Ability to analyze complex problems, develop effective solutions, and make sound administrative and operational decisions.
Ability to plan, organize, direct, and evaluate environmental health programs and personnel.
Ability to promote compliance with public health laws, regulations, and established standards.
Ability to communicate effectively with diverse audiences, including governmental officials, regulated entities, professional organizations, employees, and the public.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with employees, community partners, public health officials, and other stakeholders.
Ability to interact effectively and professionally with individuals from diverse cultural, socioeconomic, educational, racial, ethnic, and professional backgrounds.
Ability to manage competing priorities, exercise sound judgment, and maintain accountability for program performance.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in Environmental Science, Biology, Chemistry, Geology, Engineering (Agricultural, Chemical, Civil, Environmental, Mechanical, or Sanitary), or a closely related field.

Four (4) years of professional experience in environmental health, environmental enforcement, environmental protection, environmental monitoring, environmental research, or a related regulatory field.
Reliable personal vehicle, valid driver's license, and ability to travel throughout the county as required.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Experience administering environmental health programs, regulatory compliance activities, and enforcement actions.

Three (3) or more years of supervisory or management experience in environmental health or public health regulatory programs.
Registration as a Registered Environmental Health Specialist (REHS) or Registered Sanitarian (RS).
Certified Retail Food Safety Manager (CFSM or CFPM).
Standardized Food Service Establishment Inspection Officer (Standardized) or Standardized Food Service Establishment Training and Inspection Officer (District Standard Trainer).
Completion of CDC's Vector Control for Environmental Health Professionals (VCEHP) Training.
Certified Septic Level 2 Inspector.

Working Environment

Work is performed primarily in an office and field environment within the county. The position requires frequent interaction with employees, regulated businesses, government agencies, community partners, and members of the public. Field responsibilities may include visits to food service establishments, onsite sewage systems, and other environmental health sites.

The work may involve exposure to outdoor weather conditions, potentially hazardous environments, infectious or communicable diseases, chemicals, pests, and other environmental health hazards. May require occasional evening, weekend, or emergency response duties based on operational needs.

The position requires the ability to travel throughout the county, conduct site visits and inspections, attend meetings, and respond to environmental health incidents as necessary. Employees must be able to perform the essential functions of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.

### **Job Description and Duties**

Under the direction of the Nutria Eradication Operations Supervisor, the incumbent will serve as one of the lead field scientists for the Nutria Eradication Program. Nutria are highly invasive and extremely detrimental to the environment, but primarily nocturnal and relatively elusive in low densities. This position will play a critical role in the coordination of field crews conducting nutria surveys and trapping across the southern portion of the nutria infestation. The incumbent will assist the Operations Supervisor with training, leading, and evaluating field crew technicians and scientific aides to survey for, detect, and remove nutria, with the ultimate goal of eradicating nutria from the State of California. The incumbent will lead the team by example in conducting habitat suitability assessments, visual observation and camera surveys, trapping, and electronic data collection (i.e., Field Maps smartphone application), as well as effective use of baits and lures and obtaining entry permits from local landowners. The incumbent is responsible for conducting morning briefings of the assigned crew, tracking daily spatial assignments, and ensuring field staff understand understand project protocols. The incumbent will work with the Operations Supervisors, other field crew leads, and Planning Specialist to evaluate and help refine detection and trapping methods and tools for the most effective and efficient detection and removal of nutria. The incumbent will also closely coordinate with other regions and Department functions, as well as other affected and involved local, State, and Federal agencies. Work includes preparing draft reports and correspondence and answering routine questions from the public relative to Departmental nutria efforts. The primary geographical focus of this position will be in Merced, Stanislaus, Mariposa, and Fresno counties, but work may be assigned in any part of the area of nutria infestation. This position is physically demanding, but highly rewarding given the ultimate accomplishment of protecting California's wetlands, waterways, infrastructure, and agriculture from the devastation nutria have caused in other regions of North America.

Job Title: Environmental Scientist (Staff Scientist)

Job Description

This Environmental Scientist (Staff Scientist) role focuses on designing, supervising, and executing complex laboratory and field studies that assess the behavior and persistence of chemicals in the environment. The position plays a key role in delivering high-quality, regulatory-compliant environmental fate and ecotoxicology data to a global clientele across agrochemicals, industrial chemicals, pharmaceuticals, biocides, and animal health products. You will act as a technical expert, provide guidance to colleagues and clients, and contribute to the development of procedures, methods, and reports that support global regulatory submissions.

Responsibilities

Design and supervise simple and complex experiments and procedures in accordance with all applicable regulatory requirements, including but not limited to DEA, EPA, FDA, FIFRA, and OECD guidelines.
Develop procedures and methods to solve technical problems and improve laboratory practices and workflows.
Serve as a technical expert for staff and external customers, providing scientific guidance and support on environmental fate and related studies.
Perform advanced troubleshooting of instrumentation and equipment to ensure accurate and reliable data generation.
Conduct studies to determine the persistence, distribution, and behavior of chemicals in various environmental matrices such as soil, water, and other media.
Perform complex data evaluations, interpret results, and ensure scientific integrity and accuracy in all analyses.
Review the work and data generated by other staff members to ensure compliance with quality standards and regulatory requirements.
Write complex technical reports, including study reports and standard operating procedures, that clearly document methods, results, and conclusions.
Serve as a primary business contact for clients on assigned projects, providing updates, clarifying technical issues, and ensuring customer satisfaction.
Work concurrently on multiple projects, effectively prioritizing tasks and managing timelines to meet project and regulatory deadlines.
Monitor and direct activities of other staff within your area of expertise, offering technical leadership and mentoring.
Potentially serve as Study Director on one or more projects, overseeing Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) compliance and ensuring that all work on assigned projects meets regulatory and internal quality standards.
Confer with scientists and colleagues to plan research, discuss findings, and prepare technical papers and reports.
Train staff on laboratory techniques, methods, and procedures necessary to complete environmental fate and related laboratory assignments.
Maintain accurate records, follow established protocols and company policies, and support continuous improvement of laboratory operations.

Essential Skills

Demonstrated experience working in a GLP-compliant laboratory environment, including adherence to regulatory standards such as DEA, EPA, FDA, FIFRA, and OECD.
Strong Expereince in environmental science, environmental fate studies, or closely related disciplines.
Proficiency in chemistry and analytical chemistry, including chemical testing and wet chemistry techniques.
Experience in environmental fate studies that evaluate the persistence and behavior of chemicals in environmental matrices.
Working knowledge of environmental compliance and environmental field practices, including soil sampling and remediation concepts.
Familiarity with laboratory operations, quality control procedures, and environmental engineering or environmental remediation principles.
Ability to perform advanced troubleshooting of scientific instrumentation and laboratory equipment.
Strong computer skills and the ability to use scientific software and data analysis tools effectively.
Excellent scientific and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and prioritize tasks.
Excellent oral and written communication skills, including the ability to write complex technical reports and standard operating procedures.
High attention to detail and a commitment to data integrity and quality.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team, demonstrating self-motivation, adaptability, and a positive attitude.
Ability to learn new techniques, perform multiple tasks simultaneously, and maintain accurate and complete records.
Bachelors degree in a relevant field such as chemistry, biochemistry, biology, or another directly related discipline.
Minimum of five years of experience in an environmental fate laboratory with direct involvement in GLP studies.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Masters degree in a relevant field such as chemistry, biochemistry, biology, environmental science, or related discipline.
At least three years of directly relevant experience in an environmental fate laboratory when combined with a Masters degree, as a substitute for the bachelors degree plus five years of experience.
Experience in microbiology, biology, toxicology, or related life science disciplines.
Expereince in environmental engineering, environmental remediation, or related environmental fields.
Experience with analytical chemistry and wet chemistry methods applied to environmental and chemical testing.

Experience as a Study Director or in project management within a GLP laboratory environment.
Experience working with agrochemicals, industrial chemicals, pharmaceuticals, biocides, or animal health products in a testing or research setting.
